metadata.description: res.partner knowledge - customers, suppliers, location search

rules.rule: Clients: `res.partner` with at least one **posted** sales invoice (`account.move` `move_type` in `out_invoice`/`out_refund`, `state='posted'`) as invoice `partner_id` / commercial partner. NEVER `customer_rank`. NEVER `customer=True`. NEVER calendar attendees (`partner_ids`) alone. NEVER `hr.employee`.

Spoken, unsure or transposed names ("something like…"): call PRELOADED `search_by_affinity('res.partner', needles)` (optional `fields=['name','display_name','email','ref','vat']`). It hands back ranked **dicts** (`hit['id']`), not partners: `browse` those ids to read `city`, `vat`, `email` or any other column. Full-token `ilike` misses letter swaps. Do not say "no contact" until affinity returns empty.

A spoken name that returns SEVERAL plausible partners is the normal case (homonyms, branches, the parent and its contacts): return those candidates as rows (`id`, `display_name`, plus what separates them — `city`, `vat`, `email`, parent) and ask which one. Do not keep the first hit, do not pick by affinity score, and do not silently prefer the one with invoices. See the core rule on ambiguous records.

Postal address: prefer the computed field `contact_address` (single formatted string). Atomic parts: `street`, `street2`, `zip`, `city`, `state_id`, `country_id`. NEVER `contact_address_complete` (not a standard `res.partner` field; raises AttributeError). If unsure which address fields exist, check `Partner._fields` or assemble from the atomic parts.

pattern.name: clients_via_posted_invoices
pattern.description: Distinct partners that appear on posted customer invoices.
pattern.code_snippet: Move = env['account.move'] invs = Move.search([ ('move_type', 'in', ('out_invoice', 'out_refund')), ('state', '=', 'posted'), ]) clients = invs.mapped('partner_id').mapped('commercial_partner_id') # or: partner_ids = list(set(invs.mapped('partner_id').ids))

pattern.name: clients_ranked_by_calendar_events_ytd
pattern.description: Top-N clients by calendar events/visits YTD. Universe = posted-invoice clients. Standard calendar.event has no client field: discover a Many2one to res.partner that is not user_id. If none exists, say so. NEVER invent customer_id. NEVER rank partner_ids attendees as the client.

pattern.name: approx_partner_name
pattern.description: Approximate contact name. Affinity first; then client = posted invoice.
pattern.code_snippet: needles = [] # spoken tokens from this turn hits = search_by_affinity( 'res.partner', needles, fields=['name', 'display_name', 'email', 'ref', 'vat'], ) # hits are dicts: [{'id': .., 'name': .., 'score': ..}, ..] cands = env['res.partner'].browse([h['id'] for h in hits]) rows = [{ 'id': p.id, 'name': p.display_name, 'city': p.city or '', 'vat': p.vat or '', 'email': p.email or '', } for p in cands] # result = rows # If the user asked for clients, keep ids that appear on posted # out_invoice / out_refund (see clients_via_posted_invoices).

pattern.name: which_partner_did_you_mean
pattern.description: More than one plausible partner for the spoken name: deliver the candidates and ask. Never act on a guessed one.
pattern.code_snippet: Partner = env['res.partner'] # ids from affinity dicts ([h['id'] for h in hits]) or ilike cands = Partner.browse(ids) rows = [{ 'id': p.id, 'name': p.display_name, 'city': p.city or '', 'vat': p.vat or '', 'email': p.email or '', } for p in cands[:10]] # result = {'data': rows} # Then ask, in one sentence, which of them it is.
